description: The 10 product types, full commerce model, pricing tiers, revenue model, order lifecycle, entitlement model, and marketplace structure for CreatorOS

product_types.name: Community
product_types.description: Branded community spaces with text, voice, and video channels. Discord-like experience with free and paid membership tiers, channel-level permissions, and role-based gating.
product_types.pricing_note: Free tier for open communities; paid monthly/annual subscriptions for premium communities. Creator sets price.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase or free join, user is added to community member list with appropriate role. Access granted via entitlement.
product_types.implementation_note: communities and channels tables exist. Basic community CRUD and channel messaging works. No membership tiers, no payment gating, no voice/video channels, no role-based access.
examples: Paid coaching community with tiered channels

product_types.name: AI Agent
product_types.description: Custom AI agents with configurable system prompts, personality, and knowledge base. Creators build and sell AI chatbots trained on their expertise.
product_types.pricing_note: Free agents for lead gen, one-time purchase for standalone bots, or recurring subscription for ongoing AI access with token limits.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, buyer gets chat interface access to the AI agent. Token usage tracked per user.
product_types.implementation_note: ai_agents and ai_chats tables exist. AI page with AgentCard and ChatInterface components work. No pricing, no purchasing, no token tracking, no model selection.

product_types.name: Digital Download
product_types.description: Digital files sold for one-time purchase. Templates, presets, ebooks, music, art, PDFs, design assets, and any downloadable digital goods.
product_types.pricing_note: Single purchase grants perpetual download access. Optional pay-what-you-want with minimum price. No recurring billing.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase completion, buyer receives download link via order confirmation page and email. Download link is time-limited and authenticated.
product_types.implementation_note: Products table exists (generic, no type discriminator). Product creation form renders. No file upload, no download delivery, no checkout, no Stripe.

product_types.name: Course
product_types.description: Structured online learning content with modules, video lessons, quizzes, assignments, certificates, and progress tracking. Teachable-like experience within CreatorOS.
product_types.pricing_note: One-time purchase for lifetime access, or installment plans (e.g., 3x payments). Free courses supported for lead generation. No recurring subscription for individual courses.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, enrollment record created. Lessons available immediately or via drip schedule (configurable delay in days after enrollment). Progress tracked per lesson.
product_types.implementation_note: No course-related pages or components in codebase. No course, lesson, or enrollment tables in schema. Course Platform is module 3 of 16 in the PRD.

product_types.name: Subscription / Membership
product_types.description: Recurring subscription granting access to a bundle of content, community, courses, and perks. The creator's equivalent of a Patreon tier.
product_types.pricing_note: Monthly or annual billing cycle. Optional free trial period. Optional one-time setup fee. Annual discount typically 15-20% off monthly rate.
product_types.delivery_note: On subscription start, entitlements created for all included products, communities, and perks. Entitlements revoked on subscription cancellation (with optional grace period).
product_types.implementation_note: No subscription or membership tables in schema. No Stripe subscription integration. No billing portal. No tier management UI.
examples: Free newsletter membership with paid upgrade

product_types.name: Service
product_types.description: Coaching sessions, consulting calls, done-for-you services, audits, reviews, and any human-delivered service. Bookable with calendar integration.
product_types.pricing_note: Single session price or multi-session package discount. Optional deposit required at booking. Balance due before session.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, booking confirmation sent. Calendar event created (if integration active). Questionnaire sent if configured. Zoom/Meet link generated.
product_types.implementation_note: Products table serves as generic product container. Product creation form can create service-like products. No booking system, no calendar integration, no scheduling UI.

product_types.name: Event
product_types.description: Live workshops, webinars, conferences, meetups, and virtual or in-person events with ticketing, capacity limits, and attendee management.
product_types.pricing_note: Single ticket purchase with optional tier pricing (general, early bird, VIP). Free events supported. No recurring billing for events.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, ticket confirmation sent with event details. Calendar invite attached. Meeting link shared 24h before event (or immediately for recorded events).
product_types.implementation_note: No event-related pages, components, or schema tables. Events module not started.

product_types.name: Physical Product
product_types.description: Physical goods shipped to buyers. Merchandise, books, art prints, equipment, branded products. Requires inventory tracking and shipping integration.
product_types.pricing_note: Single purchase price plus shipping. Optional compare-at price for sale display. Cost tracking for margin calculation.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, order created with shipping address. Creator fulfills and provides tracking number. Buyer receives shipping confirmation and tracking updates.
product_types.entitlement_note: Physical products do not create digital entitlements. Order completion is the delivery proof. Optional digital bonus entitlements can be bundled.
product_types.implementation_note: Products table is generic with no inventory, shipping, or variant fields. No shipping integration, no fulfillment workflow, no inventory management.

product_types.name: UGC Campaign
product_types.description: User-generated content campaign briefs posted by brands/creators seeking UGC creators. Includes application flow, deliverable tracking, compensation, and content approval workflow.
product_types.pricing_note: Brand/creator pays UGC creators per approved deliverable. Platform takes a service fee. Performance bonuses optional.
product_types.delivery_note: UGC creators apply to campaign. Brand selects creators. Product shipped if physical. Creators produce content. Brand reviews and approves. Payment released on approval.
product_types.entitlement_note: UGC campaigns do not create buyer entitlements. The deliverable is content produced by the UGC creator for the brand.
product_types.implementation_note: No UGC-related pages, components, or schema tables. UGC Campaigns module (module 8 of 16 in PRD) not started.

product_types.name: Software Access
product_types.description: SaaS tool access, API keys, plugin licenses, and software subscriptions sold by creators. Grants authenticated access to external software via license keys or OAuth.
product_types.pricing_note: Monthly/annual subscription or one-time lifetime purchase. Free tier optional for freemium model. Seat-based pricing for team tools.
product_types.delivery_note: On purchase, license key generated or OAuth access granted. Buyer redirected to software with active entitlement. Usage tracked against rate limits.
product_types.implementation_note: No software access pages, components, or schema. Products table has no license key generation, no OAuth integration, no usage tracking.

commerce_model.description: End-to-end commerce system for CreatorOS marketplace and creator storefronts
commerce_model.implementation_note: Zero commerce infrastructure exists. No Stripe dependency in package.json. No payment tables in schema. No checkout flow. No billing portal.

steps.name: product_selection
steps.description: Buyer clicks 'Buy' or 'Subscribe' on product page or marketplace listing

steps.name: auth_check
steps.description: If not logged in, redirect to auth (Clerk). Return to checkout after auth.

steps.name: checkout_form
steps.description: Display order summary, collect billing info. For physical products, collect shipping address. Apply coupon/promo codes.

steps.name: payment_processing
steps.description: Stripe Checkout Session or Payment Intent created. Platform fee calculated based on creator's tier (8%/5%/3%). Stripe Connect split payment.

steps.name: payment_confirmation
steps.description: Stripe webhook confirms payment_intent.succeeded. Order status updated to 'completed'.

steps.name: entitlement_provisioning
steps.description: Entitlement record created based on product type. Access granted immediately for digital products. For services, booking flow initiated.

steps.name: order_confirmation
steps.description: Confirmation page displayed. Email sent with order details, download links (digital), booking details (services), or ticket (events).

steps.name: post_purchase
steps.description: Buyer redirected to purchased content. Creator notified of sale. Revenue dashboard updated. UMH signal emitted.

variants.free_product: Skip steps 3-5. Create order with amount_cents=0, status='completed'. Proceed to entitlement provisioning.
variants.subscription: Stripe Subscription created instead of Payment Intent. Recurring billing managed by Stripe. Webhook handles subscription lifecycle (renewal, cancellation, failed payment).
variants.physical_product: Additional shipping address collection in step 3. Fulfillment workflow after step 5 (creator ships, provides tracking).
variants.ugc_campaign: No buyer checkout. Campaign posted by brand. UGC creators apply. Payment released on deliverable approval via Stripe Connect transfer.

payment_processing.provider_note: PRD specifies Stripe Connect. Not implemented. No Stripe dependency in package.json.
payment_processing.account_note: Each creator business connects a Stripe Express account for payouts. Platform (CreatorOS) is the Connect platform.

split_payment.description: Every transaction splits between creator and platform via Stripe Connect application_fee_amount
split_payment.stripe_receives: standard processing fee (2.9% + $0.30 for US cards)

currencies.note: Creator sets product currency. Buyer sees price in product currency. Multi-currency display is future scope.

digital_downloads.note: Digital goods are non-refundable after download unless creator opts into extended refund policy

courses.note: Full refund if less than 20% of course completed within 30 days. No refund after 20% progress.

subscriptions.note: Subscriptions cancel at end of billing period. No prorated refunds. Creator can override.

services.note: Full refund if cancelled 48+ hours before scheduled session. No refund for no-shows.

events.note: Full refund 7+ days before event. 50% refund 2-7 days before. No refund within 48 hours.

physical_products.note: Full refund within 30 days of delivery. Buyer ships back at own cost. Creator can override.

processing.stripe_refund: Stripe Refund API. Funds returned to buyer's original payment method.
processing.entitlement_revocation: Entitlement status set to 'revoked' on refund completion.
processing.platform_fee_refund: Platform fee refunded proportionally. Stripe processing fee NOT refunded (Stripe policy).

open_questions: Should platform enforce a minimum refund policy or let creators set their own?
Should there be an automated dispute resolution system or manual review?
How to handle partial refunds for bundles/packages?

disputes.description: Stripe handles chargebacks. Platform needs a dispute management layer on top.

flow.description: Buyer files dispute with their bank or via platform support
Stripe notifies platform via charge.dispute.created webhook
Creator notified with dispute details and evidence request
Creator submits evidence (delivery proof, communication logs, access logs) within Stripe deadline (typically 7-21 days)
Platform submits evidence to Stripe on creator's behalf
Stripe/bank resolves dispute. Platform updates order status accordingly.

disputes.platform_responsibility: Provide creator with dispute management UI. Auto-collect evidence where possible (download logs, access logs, enrollment progress). Coach creators on evidence requirements.
disputes.dispute_fee: Stripe charges $15 per dispute. Platform absorbs or passes to creator — operator decision required.

pricing.description: 4-tier SaaS pricing for creator accounts on CreatorOS platform
pricing.discrepancy_note: Task description states Business=$79, Enterprise=$199+. PRD states Business=$99, Enterprise=custom. PRD is authoritative source. Both values preserved.

pro.name: Pro
pro.annual_note: Annual pricing not specified in PRD. $290/yr ($24.17/mo) is typical 17% annual discount.
features: Unlimited courses with all content types

business.name: Business
business.price_note: PRD says $99/mo. Task description says $79/mo. PRD is authoritative. Both preserved.
features: Team seats (up to 5 included, additional at $10/mo each)

enterprise.name: Enterprise
enterprise.price_note: PRD says custom pricing. Task description says $199+/mo. PRD is authoritative. Both preserved.

streams.description: Monthly/annual subscription revenue from creator accounts (Pro/Business/Enterprise tiers)
streams.processor: Stripe Billing (platform's own Stripe account, not Connect)
streams.margin: high — near 100% gross margin on SaaS revenue

streams.description: Percentage of every sale through the platform, tiered by creator's plan (8%/5%/3%)
streams.processor: Stripe Connect application_fee_amount on each payment
streams.margin: high — platform fee is pure revenue after Stripe's cut

streams.description: Self-serve advertising revenue from brands promoting products/content within CreatorOS feed and marketplace
Custom pricing contracts for large creator businesses and agencies
streams.margin: high — custom pricing always above standard tiers

platform_fee.description: Percentage taken from every creator sale, applied as Stripe Connect application_fee_amount

starter_free.note: Highest fee incentivizes upgrade to paid plan

payment_processing_fee.description: Stripe's standard processing fee, paid by the creator (deducted from payout)
payment_processing_fee.note: This is Stripe's fee, not CreatorOS revenue. Passed through to creator.

premium_features.description: Features gated behind paid tiers that drive subscription upgrades

revenue_model.implementation_note: Zero revenue infrastructure exists. No Stripe account, no subscription management, no transaction fee collection, no checkout flow, no billing portal, no revenue dashboard with real data.

order_lifecycle.description: State machine for order records from creation through completion, refund, or cancellation

states.description: Order created, payment not yet confirmed. Stripe PaymentIntent created but not succeeded.
Payment confirmed, entitlements being provisioned. Short-lived transitional state.
Payment confirmed, entitlements provisioned, order fulfilled. Terminal success state.
Buyer or creator initiated refund. Awaiting approval or processing.
Refund processed via Stripe. Entitlements revoked. Terminal state.
Partial refund processed (e.g., one item in a bundle). Some entitlements may remain.
Order cancelled before payment completion. No charge processed. Terminal state.
Buyer filed a chargeback with their bank. Under investigation.
Payment failed (declined card, insufficient funds). Terminal failure state.

transitions.trigger: buyer cancels or payment intent expires (30 min)
refund approved and processed via Stripe

automations.action: Send order confirmation email to buyer
Create entitlement records based on product type
Send refund confirmation email to buyer
Notify creator with evidence collection prompt
Send payment failure email to buyer with retry link

entitlement_model.description: Access control system linking purchases to product access. Every non-physical purchase creates an entitlement record.

types.grants: Access to course content, lessons, quizzes. Creates enrollment record.
Membership in community with role assignment. Access to gated channels.
Access to download digital files. Download link generation and tracking.
Access to a bundle of products, communities, and perks included in the subscription tier.
License key or OAuth token for external software. Usage tracking against rate limits.
Admission to event. Calendar invite and meeting link access.
Confirmed booking for service session(s). Calendar slot reserved.

duration_types.perpetual: Never expires. Access granted forever unless explicitly revoked (refund, admin action).
duration_types.recurring: Active while subscription is current. Checked against Stripe subscription status on each access.
duration_types.single_use: Consumed on use (event attendance, service session). Cannot be re-used.
duration_types.package_count: Decremented on each use (e.g., 5-session coaching package). Expires when count reaches 0.
duration_types.time_limited: Expires after a fixed duration (e.g., 90-day access). Checked against expires_at timestamp.

process.action: Access check middleware returns 403 for revoked entitlements
Buyer notified of access removal with reason
Associated records updated (enrollment dropped, community member removed, license deactivated)

grace_period.subscriptions: Access continues until end of current billing period even after cancellation
grace_period.failed_payments: 3 retry attempts over 7 days before entitlement revoked
grace_period.note: Grace period is configurable per product by the creator

transfer.description: Whether entitlements can be transferred between users
transfer.proposed: NOT_TRANSFERABLE by default. Creator can enable transfer for specific product types (e.g., event tickets). Transfer creates new entitlement for recipient and revokes original.
open_questions: Should gifting be supported (buy for someone else)?
Should course access be transferable within a team?

access_check.description: How the system determines if a user can access gated content

flow.description: User requests gated resource (course lesson, community channel, download link)
Middleware queries entitlements table: user_id + product_id + status='active' + (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW())
If entitlement found and valid: grant access. If not: return 403 with upgrade/purchase prompt.
For subscriptions: additionally verify Stripe subscription status is active (webhook-driven, cached in entitlement status)

marketplace.description: Product discovery, search, and browsing experience for consumers on CreatorOS

mechanisms.description: Consumer feed shows products from followed creators alongside content posts. Algorithm ranks by relevance, recency, and engagement.
Dedicated marketplace page with category navigation, featured products, and trending listings.
Each creator has a storefront page listing all their products organized by type.
AI-powered recommendations based on purchase history, browsing behavior, and similar creators.
Products surfaced based on purchases by people you follow, trending in your communities, and review ratings.

search.scope: All published products across all creators on the platform
features: Full-text search across product name, description, and tags
Sort by: relevance, newest, price low-to-high, price high-to-low, best selling, highest rated
Creator search (find products by specific creator)
search.implementation_note: Marketplace page exists with basic product listing. No search, no filters, no sorting. ProductCard and ProductList components render but with no interaction.

categories.description: Product categories for marketplace navigation. Creator selects category when creating product.
categories.note: Categories are currently a free-text field on the products table. No enum enforcement. No category table.

reviews.description: Product review and rating system for marketplace trust and discovery

model.verified_purchase: Boolean — only buyers with completed orders can leave reviews
model.helpful_votes: Other users can mark reviews as helpful
model.creator_response: Creator can respond to each review once

reviews.implementation_note: Products table has rating and review_count columns (denormalized) but no reviews table exists. No review submission UI. No review display on product pages.

ratings.calculation: Average of all verified-purchase review ratings. Displayed as X.X stars with review count.
ratings.display: Product cards show star rating + review count. Product pages show full review breakdown (5-star distribution).
ratings.minimum_reviews: Products with 0 reviews show 'New' badge instead of stars. Rating displayed after 3+ reviews.
ratings.fraud_prevention: Only verified purchasers can review. One review per user per product. Reviews moderated for spam/abuse.

open_questions.question: Confirm Stripe Connect as sole payment processor, or evaluate alternatives (PayPal, Square, Lemonsqueezy)?
open_questions.recommendation: Stripe Connect is the industry standard for marketplace/platform payments. PRD specifies it. No reason to deviate unless operator has specific requirements.
open_questions.impact: All checkout, payout, subscription, and refund flows depend on this choice.

open_questions.question: Should the platform enforce a minimum refund policy, or let each creator set their own refund terms?
open_questions.recommendation: Platform-enforced minimum (e.g., 14-day for digital, 30-day for courses <20% complete) with creator ability to offer MORE generous terms. This protects consumers and platform reputation.
open_questions.impact: Affects buyer trust, creator flexibility, dispute rates, and platform ToS.

open_questions.question: How will sales tax / VAT be handled? Stripe Tax? Third-party (TaxJar, Avalara)? Creator responsibility?
open_questions.recommendation: Stripe Tax for simplicity — auto-calculates and collects tax based on buyer location. Included in checkout flow. Platform remits or creator remits depending on MoR (Merchant of Record) model.
open_questions.impact: Legal compliance. Affects checkout flow, pricing display (tax-inclusive vs exclusive), and financial reporting. Must be resolved before any public commerce launch.

open_questions.question: What currencies will be supported at launch? Multi-currency pricing or single currency with conversion?
open_questions.recommendation: USD-only at launch. Add multi-currency pricing as a Business/Enterprise tier feature. Stripe handles currency conversion for international buyers automatically.
open_questions.impact: Affects product creation flow (price field per currency vs single price), checkout display, and creator payout currency.

open_questions.question: Is CreatorOS the Merchant of Record (MoR) or is each creator their own MoR?
open_questions.recommendation: Each creator is their own MoR via Stripe Connect Express accounts. Platform is the facilitator, not the seller. This simplifies tax liability — each creator is responsible for their own tax obligations. Platform provides 1099-K reporting data.
open_questions.impact: Fundamental business model decision. Affects tax liability, refund processing, legal risk, Stripe Connect account type, and platform ToS.

open_questions.question: Who pays the $15 Stripe dispute fee — the platform or the creator?
open_questions.recommendation: Creator pays dispute fees (deducted from next payout). This incentivizes creators to maintain quality and resolve issues before they become chargebacks. Platform absorbs first dispute as goodwill.
open_questions.impact: Affects creator payout calculation and creator ToS.

open_questions.question: Should the free tier have a maximum monthly GMV (gross merchandise volume) before forcing upgrade?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes — cap free tier at $1,000/mo GMV. Creators exceeding this clearly have a viable business and should upgrade. The 8% transaction fee alone makes this profitable, but the cap encourages subscription revenue.
open_questions.impact: Affects free tier economics and upgrade conversion rate.

open_questions.question: Should purchased access be transferable (gifting, resale, team sharing)?
open_questions.recommendation: Not transferable by default. Enable gifting (buy-for-someone-else) as a checkout option. Event tickets transferable. No resale marketplace (avoid scalping). Team sharing via Business tier team seats.
open_questions.impact: Affects entitlement model complexity, potential for abuse, and revenue (transfers bypass platform fees on resale).

open_questions.question: Should Clerk auth migration happen before or after commerce tables? Auth is P0 security (broken passwords). Commerce is P0 revenue.
open_questions.recommendation: Auth first. The broken comparePasswords vulnerability means any deployed commerce would be exploitable. Fix auth, then build commerce on the secure foundation.
open_questions.impact: If auth first: all commerce code uses Clerk from day 1. If commerce first: commerce code must be rewritten when auth migrates.

open_questions.question: PRD says Business=$99/mo, Enterprise=custom. Task inputs say Business=$79, Enterprise=$199+. Which is canonical?
open_questions.recommendation: PRD is the original operator-authored source. Use PRD values ($99, custom) unless operator explicitly overrides.
open_questions.impact: Affects pricing page, Stripe product configuration, and revenue projections.
